figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Structural and biosynthetic features of vinigrol (1) and
fungal diterpenoids. (A) Chemical structure of 1. Common
bicyclo[5.3.1]undecane skeletons of 1 and taxane are highlighted by
red bold lines in the respective carbon skeletons. (B) Selected
examples of fungal diterpenoids. (C) Nature’s strategy for the
biosynthesis of 1 proposed in this study.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Heterologous biosynthesis of 1. (A) The biosynthetic gene
cluster for 1 in V. nigra F-5408. (B) LC−MS analysis of the culture
broth of constructed transformants. Chromatograms monitoring the
total ion current (TIC) are shown.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. ColabFold-based structural analysis of VigB. (A) Structural comparison of VigB (ColabFold model) and CLM1 (PDB ID: 8H4P). (B)
Comparison of CLM1 and VigB. (C) Schematic representation of the barrel structures of CLM1 and VigB. In (B) and (C), the corresponding α
helices are shown in the same colors. Small α helices (α1, 2, 4, 5 of CLM1, α1−3, α5 of VigB) are omitted for clarity.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. Functional characterization of the terpene cyclase VigB. (A) GC-MS analysis of the mycelial extracts of the transformants. (B) GC−MS
analysis of the enzymatic reactions of VigB and its mutants. The activity of most of the mutants involved in substrate binding was abolished. The
trace activity of the Y436A mutant might be explained by its lower importance in other TSs.37 (C) Schematic representation of the domain
organization of VigB and CLM1. Consensus sequence Logos generated by Weblogo38 for the four conserved motifs are shown. (D) Close-up view
of the putative active sites of VigB and CLM1.
